An Amazon developer pointed to an Amazon contribution to the Sentry repo and said many developers at Amazon love(d) using Sentry, and one wanted to contribute back in a small way.

Self-hosted Sentry kept growing: each release unleashed more containers and consumed more memory until they couldn't run anything on their 32GB server except Sentry. They evaluated GlitchTip and Bugsink and moved to GlitchTip.
A team running Sentry and GlitchTip side by side found GlitchTip has many more bugs than Sentry, but they are trying to stick with it because it is so much lighter.

GlitchTip replaced their Sentry 9.x ("pre-Clickhouse madness") by just updating the DSN in configs. Its UI is a bit buggy, but it does 99% of what Sentry did with 10% of the effort needed to maintain a modern Sentry setup.
With a small user base (<1000 users), Sentry did not make sense for them. GlitchTip lacks some of Sentry's functionality but covers their needs and has run in production for a year without problems.

A user who loves Sentry said that for a growing business its features are more nice-to-have than critical, and the hosted monthly bill is easy to rack up. They appreciated that self-hosting gives an escape hatch so heavy Sentry integration isn't complete vendor lock-in.

Huge Sentry fans with it deeply integrated in their products: the fully open source code helped a ton with advanced integrations, since they could see exactly what happens instead of relying only on the docs (which are also great). They plan to keep using Sentry despite the BSL change.

They have run self-hosted Sentry at work for a couple of years and it has worked fantastically; once running it is rock-solid. They also use the SaaS. Self-hosted releases take time to appear after SaaS launches.
A happy user on the cloud offering in their early stages likes knowing they can host their own instance if the costs become too much.
Disappointed by the relicensing: they had planned to use Sentry for a side project but now will find an alternative or use an old version, because they refuse to rely on closed-source software.
